amenities.cold_plunge: Victoria's cold plunge culture sits within a broader European bathhouse tradition that has taken hold gradually in Australian cities. Cold immersion pools — maintained well below ambient temperature, typically fed by chilled water systems rather than natural sources — are the point around which many contemporary bathhouse circuits are built. Sense of Self in Collingwood is currently the sole listed venue in this state carrying the amenity.
amenities.infrared_sauna: Victoria's bathhouse scene is modest in number but deliberate in offering, and infrared saunas have become one of its more quietly sought amenities. Unlike traditional steam or dry-heat saunas, infrared saunas use radiant heat absorbed directly by the body rather than warming the surrounding air. Soak Bathhouse in South Yarra is currently the sole listed venue in the state carrying this amenity.
amenities.led_therapy: LED light therapy uses specific wavelengths of light — most commonly red and near-infrared — applied to the skin to support cellular processes, without heat or UV exposure. Victoria's listing for this amenity is currently a single venue: Soak Bathhouse in South Yarra. The short list reflects how selectively this technology tends to appear within bathhouse settings, where it usually sits alongside rather than at the centre of a broader water-based offering.
amenities.magnesium_pool: Magnesium pools use water saturated with magnesium chloride rather than the sodium chloride of seawater or the calcium compounds of hard tap water — the mineral is absorbed transdermally, though the degree of uptake remains a subject of ongoing physiological research. Victoria's listing in this category is currently a single entry: Sense of Self in Collingwood.
amenities.traditional_sauna: Victoria's bathhouse offering with a traditional sauna is, at present, a short list — Sense of Self in Collingwood standing as the single entry. A traditional sauna operates on dry or low-humidity heat, typically wood-fired or electrically heated, distinct from steam rooms or infrared cabinets. Whether the category grows is a matter of record; this page reflects what is documented now.

VIC.state: Victoria's bathhouse culture is modest by international measure, though it has been gathering definition in recent years. Sense of Self in Collingwood currently represents the state's indexed offering — a single venue does not make a tradition, but it marks a starting point from which the category can be tracked over time.

categories.bathhouse: Bathhouses occupy a distinct position among bathing venues: they are typically built around communal water facilities — pools, plunge baths, steam rooms — drawing on Central European and Scandinavian bathing traditions rather than the treatment-room model of a day spa. Both Aurora Spa & Bathhouse in Sorrento and Sense of Self in Collingwood sit within this category, where the water circuit itself is the main event rather than a backdrop to bookable services.
categories.day_spa: Day spas sit at the practical end of the bathing spectrum — typically built around treatment rooms rather than communal pools, with an emphasis on booked sessions over open bathing time. This national listing brings together day spas from across Australia, with Chuan Spa in Southbank among those currently indexed.
categories.thermal_springs: Thermal springs draw water from underground — geothermal or artesian sources — and the mineral content and temperature of that water varies considerably depending on the geology of the site. Alba Thermal Springs & Spa in Fingal represents Victoria's growing interest in purpose-built bathing facilities centred on naturally sourced water, a form of bathing with a long European and Japanese precedent that has taken root more recently in the Australian context.
